device.description: 12-bit 250 kSPS sampling ADC, +/-10 V input, 12-bit or byte-wide parallel bus with R/C, BYTE and BUSY
device.note: ads8504.pdf (SLAS434A) p.3 electrical characteristics (logic levels, binary twos complement, bus access/relinquish 83 ns), p.4 VDIG 4.75-5.25 V, DW pinout, p.5 terminal functions, p.8-9 basic operation, starting a conversion, Table 1 control line functions, reading data, p.10 Table 2 output codes, Table 3 conversion timing, p.11 Figure 18 bit locations vs BYTE

notModeled: analog input (+/-10 V), internal/external reference and CAP: the result is always the 0 V code 000h (twos complement)

pins 19-22 (all named DZ): LOW with BYTE low, bits 7..4 (pin 19 = bit 7 ... pin 22 = bit 4) with BYTE high (Figure 18); four pins with the same name cannot be bus data pins, so they are never driven and the BYTE-high read models only D11-D0 (pins 6-9 = bits 3..0, pins 10-13 LOW, pins 15-18 = bits 11..8)

conversion start: CS and R/C are internally ORed and level triggered (both low >= 40 ns starts conversion n, whichever falls last); the model starts one on every R/C falling edge and ignores a start by CS falling while R/C is low
a new convert command while BUSY is low aborts the conversion in progress and resets the ADC (Table 1, Figure 22)
reading the previous result during a conversion (valid up to t2 after the start) and invalid data from then until BUSY rises: the model always outputs the 0 V code while R/C is high and CS is low
BUSY delays tpd 25 ns / td1, acquisition time 1.8 us, convert pulse width 40-1750 ns, VDIG <= VANA
variants: single-device datasheet; pin-compatible with ADS7804 (100 kSPS) and the 16-bit ADS8505.
